question: A 9-month-old girl is brought to the physician by her parents for multiple episodes of unresponsiveness in which she stares blankly and her eyelids flutter. She has gradually lost control of her neck and ability to roll over during the past 2 months. She is startled by loud noises and does not maintain eye contact. Her parents are of Ashkenazi Jewish descent. Neurological examination shows generalized hypotonia. Deep tendon reflexes are 3+ bilaterally. Fundoscopy shows bright red macular spots bilaterally. Abdominal examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following metabolites is most likely to accumulate due to this patient's disease?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Deficiency in lysosomal enzyme activity -> Accumulation of specific metabolites -> 90% CHAIN: Ashkenazi Jewish descent -> Increased risk of lysosomal storage disorders -> 80% CHAIN: Generalized hypotonia and loss of motor skills -> Neurological dysfunction -> 85% CHAIN: Bright red macular spots on fundoscopy -> Suggestive of cherry-red spot -> 95% CHAIN: Unresponsiveness, eyelid fluttering, and startle response to loud noises -> Neurological symptoms -> 80% CHAIN: Deep tendon reflexes 3+ bilaterally -> Indication of neurological dysfunction -> 75% CHAIN: Accumulation of GM2 ganglioside -> Tay-Sachs disease -> 90%
analysis: The clinical presentation of the 9-month-old girl with episodes of unresponsiveness, loss of motor skills, hypotonia, and bright red macular spots is suggestive of Tay-Sachs disease, which is more common in individuals of Ashkenazi Jewish descent. Tay-Sachs disease is characterized by a deficiency of the enzyme hexosaminidase A, leading to the accumulation of GM2 ganglioside in the central nervous system.
